chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Husayn ibn 'Umar ibn Yazid, from his father, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When the two traders are truthful and sincere, blessings are bestowed upon them; but when they lie and cheat, blessings are not bestowed upon them. And they both have the option to cancel the deal as long as they have not parted. If they differ, then the word of the owner of the goods prevails, or they may cancel the deal."

key_terms.الْخِيَار: the option/right to choose (to confirm or cancel)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on lying and cheating in trade according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the spiritual dimension of trade, linking commercial integrity directly to divine barakah. It codifies the principle of *Khiyar al-Majlis*, granting both parties the right to rescind the contract while in the same session, thereby preventing hasty or deceptive commitments. This narration serves as a foundational text in Shia jurisprudence for ensuring fairness and transparency in market transactions.
